why: Rule 1 never fires (all prongs flat); the only real Bragg is the 145k spike at 17000 that falls to MIP in 1.5 cm, making 17002 the start of that stopping pi+, but two rival hot knots (deg-3 92086 and the 17000/89072 pair 4.4 cm apart) fit the charge just as well.

Rule 1 at a deg-5 junction: four of five prongs point away and p4 shows the 20.9 cm muon climbing monotonically over its last 10 cm to 315k at 13002 on the template, plus a 19.9 cm prong rising to 230k at 13007; the 68 cm shower of cluster 81 also starts 4.7 cm away.

Rule 1 at a deg-4 junction with nothing rising toward it: p4 shows the 20.7 cm proton climbing steadily along the proton template to 255k at 16004, the 43 cm muon flat and exiting forward at z=500, and a second stopping end at 16005; a 0.9 cm proton stub sits on the vertex itself.

Rule 1 at the event's only junction, deg-4 with nothing rising toward it: p4 shows the proton prong climbing 60k to 145k over 5 cm away from 12004 while the three e prongs are flat-to-away, and the zoom shows four prongs in genuinely different directions.

Rule 7 plus rule 2: 5004 is the deg-3 apex at the extreme upstream end (z=6.3) of an 87 cm fragmented chain whose downstream blobs spread over 15 cm in y in p1, and its third prong leaves at 107 deg, though the 4.1 cm prong is 160 deg from the pion so the collinearity trap costs a tier.

Rule 1 fires 2 of 2 and p4 backs it: one prong climbs monotonically over its last 6 cm to 195k on the stopping-muon template, the other has a 305k proton-like tip, and the middle is cool, which one particle cannot do; 177 deg collinearity drops it from certain.

Rule 1 and rule 2 both name 9001 as the cool, lower-z end of the only structure in the event, and a 1.1 cm stub 2.4 cm off the far end reads as a Michel or delta, but p4 shows that far end is a 2-point 215k patch collapsing to MIP within 2 cm rather than a monotone Bragg, so it could equally be a vertex blob.

Rule 1 with p4 confirming the shape: the lone 16.5 cm segment climbs monotonically over its last 3 cm to 175k on the stopping-muon template at 2001, so 2001 is the Bragg end and 2000 the start; rule 2 mildly disagrees but is only a tiebreak.

Rule 1 fires 2 of 2 with both far ends showing genuine Bragg shapes in p4 (34 cm muon flat then climbing to 230k at 3001, 11.6 cm hadron with a 180k tip at 3000) and a cool middle; the 168 deg prong pair costs one tier.

The 275 cm muon is flat for 250 cm then shows a textbook Bragg to 240k at 17001, so the far end is the stop, and at 17004 a 105-degree branch meets it inside a ~5 cm orange vertex blob (165k and 162k tips on both segments) far too wide a kink for scattering.

Rule 2 plus topology with rule 1 silent: 5004 is the lowest-z end (z=5.8) of the whole structure and the zoom shows three prongs in distinct directions there (2.6 cm pion stub at 2 MIP, 2.8 cm stub at 83 deg), whereas the rival 5003 is where the 23.6 cm track terminates and shatters into stubs; the p5 cone test separates nothing (far-near 0.0 at every apex).

Rules 1, 2 and 3 agree: the 49.8 cm muon rises away from 26006 to a 145k template Bragg at 26008 which also carries a 4.5 cm Michel, so that end is the far one, and 26006 is the lowest-z candidate; the rival 110 cm line is flat at both ends and through-going.
Rule 8 abstain: the event is six sub-centimetre blobs scattered across the whole detector with no segment over 0.6 cm, no junction and no dQ/dx panels, so there is no readable direction to decide on.

Rule 1 points at 16000 because the interior end 16001 is the hotter one (x1.64) and 16000 sits exactly on the bottom face where a track cannot stop, but the 229 cm profile is spiky with 150k deltas throughout so the Bragg is not clean, and rule 2 prefers 16001 by 208 cm.
